Ehm... My view om a point made earlier: I suggest always to include error covariances because it is crucial to show how the model is estimated, every single path. (But a diagram can include nothing but latents if measurement models are shown elsewhere, for instance in a table, including correlated errors.)

Path models probably have to be drawn by hand, I know no software that draws good diagrams. For tables, I find xtable very flexible. But I too am curious about the most convenient way to develop tables from SEM analyses

messages.author: cb2fce509d78143e
messages.subject: Re: Export results from lavaan...How?
parts:
Ilaria,

Yes, that's a lot. It sounds like you're doing a mediation model using lavaan to test whether a model with a direct path is better than a model without the direct path. Is this correct?

If so, you would have to report the following at a minimum:

1. Model fit statistics for both models
2. Chi-square difference test
3. All paths in your most significant model.
4. Estimated variance explained in your variables.
5. If using latent variables, a measurement model where you say whether you have good measurement or not.

In terms of best practices, what the other two posters have said to include should also be included as well.

Kline has a textbook that discusses reporting practices in SEM. Others have some as well online. Yes, it is a lot to report, but doing so gives the full picture. Alternatively, you can see recent published articles using the same technique that you are using and see what they report.
